name: bounded_context_design
observations: TGv3 separates QuestionnaireSeed (consultation-captured metadata driving printable generation) from TrustData (canonical post-fill model consumed by generators/validators). These are distinct bounded contexts with different concerns, different lifecycles, and different validation regimes.

The promote_seed() function is the explicit one-way translation bridge. Seed fields that have TrustData counterparts project forward; seed-only concerns (paralegal identity, print options, accessibility overrides) are dropped.

Rationale: the paralegal's consultation workflow serves a different domain concern than the post-fill legal record. A single model with conditional validation would conflate the two contexts and force TrustData to admit invalid states (e.g., an allegedly-complete trust with no grantor name).

Parsers (docx, pdf, json) fill INTO a seed-initialized TrustData rather than constructing one from scratch. The seed-initialized instance arrives from promote_seed(seed); parsers honor the one-shot-initializer invariant by never re-invoking promote_seed, mutating the target TrustData per the post-promotion protocol.

name: person_reference_hierarchy
observations: PersonReference is the shared base for every person-like entity: full_legal_name (validator: 2+ tokens), optional date_of_birth, optional Address, phone, email, notes, is_entity, entity_name.

Derived chain: Beneficiary extends PersonReference adding disinherit+disinherit_reason; Child/Descendant/OtherBeneficiary extend Beneficiary adding relationship axes; SuccessorTrustee/CorporateTrustee extend PersonReference adding trustee-specific fields.

PersonReference carries is_minor_as_of(ref_date: date) -> bool as a computed method. Minor status is never stored; reference date policy is trust_execution_date primary, questionnaire_fill_date fallback.
Entity support: is_entity=True indicates legal entities (corporate trustees, charitable remainders, insurance companies). Such entries populate entity_name and typically omit date_of_birth.

name: address_model
observations: Structured Address Pydantic model: street, city, state, zip_code, country (default 'US'), optional latitude, optional longitude. is_populated() method checks for any field content.
Geocoding via geopy library wrapping Nominatim (public OSM endpoint). Rate-limited to 1 req/sec on free tier.
Used by PersonReference.address (optional), RealProperty.address (required). Structured form enables downstream validation and mail-merge.

name: added_models
observations: Pet: pet-trust data under Illinois 760 ILCS 3/408. Fields: name, species, distinguishing_features, microchip_id, designated_caretaker_ref, successor_caretaker_ref, care_instructions, funding_amount, annual_allowance, residual_distribution.

GuardianshipDesignation: guardianship for minor beneficiaries. Distinguishes guardian-of-person (physical care) from guardian-of-estate (property management). Fields: minor_child_ref, guardian_of_person_ref, successor_guardian_of_person_ref, guardian_of_estate_ref, successor_guardian_of_estate_ref, instructions.
DigitalAssetDirective: directive for digital asset handling under Illinois RUFADAA (755 ILCS 70). Fields: asset_type (enum), service_provider, access_instruction (enum), notes.

CustomTerm: categorized custom provisions replacing v2.2's three text-block fields. Fields: category (enum: DISTRIBUTION/BENEFICIARY/TRUSTEE_POWER/ADMINISTRATION/OTHER), content, manual_review (default True).
All *_ref fields use the reference-by-id pattern pointing into TrustData's people lists rather than duplicating identity data.

name: modified_surfaces
observations: exclusions free-text field REMOVED from TextBlocks; superseded by Beneficiary.disinherit (intake-as-election).
Three custom-text fields (custom_distribution_terms, custom_beneficiary_terms, additional_notes) COLLAPSED into TrustData.custom_terms: list[CustomTerm] with category tagging.

BeneficiaryShare and SpecificBequest adopt reference-or-external pattern: exactly one of recipient_ref (id into TrustData people lists) or recipient_external (inline PersonReference) must be populated; model_validator enforces.
WithdrawalStep typed: age:int, percent:Decimal, description:str. Replaces v2.2's free-text step/timing/percentage strings.
Incapacity provisions ADDED as TextBlocks.incapacity_provisions field (free-text, manual review).
External exclusions: list[PersonReference] on TrustData for persons explicitly excluded but not in beneficiary lists; separate from Beneficiary.disinherit.

name: party_naming
observations: Canonical schema fields: grantor (always present) and co_grantor (optional, present when trust_type=JOINT or marital_status=MARRIED).
Captions as first-class fields: grantor_caption and co_grantor_caption on TrustIdentity. Resolve to 'Grantor'/'Spouse' for individual+married or 'Grantor A'/'Grantor B' for joint.
Dissolves v2.2's husband/wife/party_a/party_b naming. Generator reads captions rather than deriving from trust_type alone, enabling firm override if local convention differs.

Parser obligation on trust_type mutation: when fill mutates trust_id.trust_type, the parser calls _resolve_captions(new_trust_type) and updates both grantor_caption and co_grantor_caption to the helper's output, preserving caption-trust_type consistency at the parser boundary.

name: ssn_collection
observations: Last-four digits only collection on GrantorInfo.ssn_last_four. Validator enforces exactly-four-digit constraint.
Data minimization principle: full SSN lives in the EIN application workflow, not the trust tool.
Supersedes PR #8/#9 (sensitive-text masking approach). Once truncated at input, masking becomes irrelevant.

name: minor_status_computation
observations: Minor status computed from date_of_birth via PersonReference.is_minor_as_of(ref_date: date) -> bool. Never stored.
Reference date policy: trust execution date (trust_id.execution_date) primary; questionnaire fill date fallback when execution date not yet set.
Callers resolve the reference date and pass it in. Generator computes at render time; GUI displays 'currently N' using date.today(); trust document uses 'as of execution date' classification.

name: relationship_enum_design
observations: Three-tier pattern: GenericRelationship holds shared members (CHILD, SIBLING, PARENT, SPOUSE, GRANDCHILD, NIECE, NEPHEW, AUNT, UNCLE, COUSIN); _ChildRelationship and _TrusteeRelationship hold scoped-only members; PEP 695 type aliases union shared and scoped where contexts need both.
_ChildRelationship values: BIOLOGICAL, ADOPTED, STEPCHILD, FOSTER. _TrusteeRelationship values: FRIEND, ATTORNEY, ACCOUNTANT, CORPORATE, OTHER.
Type aliases: ChildRelationship = _ChildRelationship; TrusteeRelationship = GenericRelationship | _TrusteeRelationship; DescendantRelationship = GenericRelationship.

Downstream resolution — value.value comparison methodology: enum equality checks use .value string comparison, never isinstance, because PEP 695 type aliases are type-checker-visible only, not runtime classes. This is forced by the three-tier design, not an independent convention.

BiologicalParent is a separate enum (BOTH, GRANTOR_ONLY, CO_GRANTOR_ONLY, OTHER) used alongside ChildRelationship — two-axis model disambiguates cases like 'stepchild later adopted by non-biological parent' (relationship becomes ADOPTED; biological_parent stays OTHER).

name: diagnostics_design
observations: Diagnostic Pydantic class: level (DiagnosticLevel enum: INFO/WARNING/ERROR), code (stable string identifier), message (human-readable), optional field_path (dotted path into TrustData for GUI anchor), source (DiagnosticSource enum: SCHEMA/BUSINESS_RULE/EXTRACTION), context (DiagnosticContext enum: FILL/GENERATE/BOTH).
Never persisted on TrustData. Computed by diagnose(trust: TrustData, config: FirmConfig) -> list[Diagnostic] at boundaries between fill, generate, and validation stages.
Diagnostic codes namespace convention: dotted lowercase like 'estate.crossed_cliff', 'shares.sum_not_100', 'trustee.none_named'. Codes are stable identifiers; messages may be rewritten for clarity.

Code namespace is split by authorship: builtin rules shipped in-repo use <domain>.<name> codes (e.g., estate.crossed_cliff); custom rules authored firm-side use custom.<topic>.<name> codes. The loader enforces the split (rejecting cross-prefix violations as DiagnosticConfigError) and performs two distinct checks at load time: code collision (two rules with the same code, within-set or across-set) raises DiagnosticConfigError as an identity violation; expression dedupe (a custom rule whose (whitespace-stripped_expression, level) matches a builtin) silently drops the custom rule with builtin winning and emits a Python logging.INFO entry naming both. Promotion of a custom rule to a builtin is a deliberate maintainer step: rewrite code prefix from custom. to <domain>., move the rule into builtin.yaml, ship in the next bundled update.

name: diagnostics_enforcement
observations: Production blocking: hard block on ERROR-level diagnostics. Forcible override available via explicit action requiring free-text reason from user; override action writes audit log entry with timestamp, user, TrustData reference, overridden diagnostic codes, and reason.
CLI flags: --restriction-level={info|warning|error} raises effective blocking threshold (default error); --force-generation convenience flag bypasses all levels.
Audit log: JSON-lines format, firm-config-specified directory, monthly rotation.

Custom rule evaluation: rules authored declaratively in YAML files in firm-config rules directory; rule-engine library evaluates expressions against TrustData + FirmConfig context. Per-rule toggle; GUI-manageable pane planned for rule administration.

Per-rule enabled: bool in the YAML rule definition is the v3 rule-disable mechanism. A firm-level toggle table in firm.toml was considered and deferred per YAGNI given the single-maintainer config model; if operational pressure surfaces (multiple paralegals requiring per-host overrides without YAML edits), the future addition is a [diagnostics.rules] table in firm.toml mapping rule-code to bool, layered above the YAML enabled field.

Forward dependency from firm_config_loader: the diagnostics engine plan must add a subscriber that captures SharedConfigStalenessWarning and SharedConfigIntegrityWarning and writes audit-log entries containing timestamp, resolved shared path, cache path, cache age, warning category, and (for integrity events) truncated parse-error reason. Subscription mechanism is logging.getLogger('py.warnings').addHandler(...) paired with logging.captureWarnings(True) at the loader's module-import time. The chore must additionally pin a target latency for 'maintainer learns of integrity-fallback event'; the value is operationally chosen by the diagnostics-engine plan author. This subscriber is a NEW audit-record category alongside the existing override-record audit log already documented in this entity's observation #1.

name: elections_design
observations: Elections Pydantic class aggregates all checkbox and enum choices from questionnaire Sections 3C, 6-10. Defaults reflect Illinois-law common practice with client-protective choice selected where options differ in protection.
Section 3A initial trustee composition: initial_trustee (InitialTrustee enum: GRANTORS/GRANTOR_ONLY/CO_GRANTOR_ONLY/OTHER).
Section 3C trustee powers: allow_trustee_coappoint (bool), allow_corporate_fiduciary (bool), corporate_fiduciary_min_capital (Decimal, default 50000).
Section 4 gating: estate_value_estimate (EstateValueRange enum: BELOW_THRESHOLD/ABOVE_THRESHOLD/DECLINED_TO_ESTIMATE), estate_value_approximate (optional Decimal).
Section 5: distribution_standard (HEMS/BROAD). Section 6: beneficiary_death (enum), remote_contingent (enum: INTESTACY/CHARITY/OTHER), remote_contingent_other (str).
Section 7: tangible_distribution (EQUAL_CHILDREN/EQUAL_BENEFICIARIES), division_method (TRUSTEE/LOTTERY/SELL).
Section 8: retirement_strategy (POD/TRUST/MIX), insurance_strategy (SPOUSE_THEN_CHILDREN/TO_TRUST/OTHER), insurance_strategy_other (str).

Section 9 protective elections: surviving_amendment (FULL/LIMITED/IRREVOCABLE), power_of_appointment (GENERAL/LIMITED/NONE), no_contest (bool, default True), spendthrift (default True), probate_coordination (default True), portability (default True), trustee_bond (default False).

Section 10: dispute_resolution (MEDIATION_ARBITRATION/COURT), trustee_compensation (REASONABLE/NONE_FAMILY/FIXED_ANNUAL/OTHER) with companion trustee_compensation_amount and trustee_compensation_other fields.

Guardianship policy: dual-behavior election guardianship_policy (DELEGATE_TO_TRUSTEES/EXPLICIT_DESIGNATIONS). Default via firm_config; shipped default EXPLICIT_DESIGNATIONS. When EXPLICIT, TrustData.guardianship_designations list is populated.
Digital assets: digital_assets_handling Literal['include_default','opt_in_per_client','omit'] with default 'include_default'.

name: estate_thresholds
observations: Illinois cliff structure (as of April 2026): soft $3M single / $6M joint (detail-collection gate); hard $4M single / $8M joint (cliff); approaching-cliff diagnostic fires at 90% of hard threshold.
Values stored in firm_config, not hardcoded. Firm updates config when legal landscape changes.
Pending legislation: HB2601 proposes raising Illinois exemption to $8M effective 2026; farm-specific bill proposes $6M for qualifying estates. Neither enacted as of April 2026.
Cliff behavior is the legal motivation: Illinois taxes the entire excess above threshold, not marginal amounts, creating non-linear exposure for estates near the line.
Threshold values configurable-not-scraped by design: auto-scraping from IRS or Illinois AG sites introduces brittleness; attorneys track legislative status manually and update config.

name: corporate_trustee_catalog
observations: SQLite-backed cache of FDIC-listed institutions with trust powers. Data sourced from FDIC Institution Directory API (banks.data.fdic.gov/api).
Geographic query by radius: 100mi implicit default, firm_config.trustee_catalog.radius_miles override. Office location from firm_config.
Refresh cadence: 30 days. Background-checked on GUI launch; paralegal sees cached data immediately while update runs.
CorporateTrustee model extends PersonReference with is_entity=True, fdic_cert_id (optional), has_trust_powers flag, last_verified date.
Non-FDIC trust companies (some state-chartered institutions) fall back to free-text entry; GUI always permits free-text even when selector is offered.

name: printable_variants
observations: 18 total variants = 6 base (trust_type × marital_status × estate_value_estimate) × 3 child-count tiers (NONE / ONE_TO_FIVE / SIX_PLUS).
QuestionnaireSeed drives variant selection at print-generation time via variant_key property: format 'trust_type_marital_status_estate_value_child_count_tier'.
Overlays (pets, explicit guardianship, digital assets) add sections additively per variant, not multiplicatively. Total variants stay at 18 regardless of overlay combinations.
Implementation cost is linear in conditional blocks, not variant count. Adding the child-count tiering costs ~15% on top of six-variant base work.
Accessibility-first design: 14-16pt Arial minimum, generous line-height, high-contrast rendering, larger checkboxes. Client base is elderly; paper is primary surface.

name: scope_envelope
observations: IN scope for v3: pets (pet trusts under 760 ILCS 3/408); guardianship designations for minor beneficiaries; digital asset directives under Illinois RUFADAA (755 ILCS 70); incapacity provisions as a TextBlocks field.

OUT scope for v3: burial/cremation/funeral preferences (handled as separate instruments by the firm); charitable lead trusts; charitable remainder trusts (advanced structured-giving vehicles, rare for firm's typical clients).
Enum expansions committed: InsuranceStrategy adds TO_TRUST + OTHER (v2.2 had only SPOUSE_THEN_CHILDREN); TrusteeCompensation adds NONE_FAMILY + FIXED_ANNUAL + OTHER; RemoteContingent adds OTHER.

Rationale pattern: items are included when firm already handles them in existing practice and when Illinois statute recognizes them (760 ILCS 3/408 for pet trusts, 755 ILCS 70 for digital assets). Items are excluded when firm handles them separately or when the legal complexity exceeds v3's firm-alpha scope.

name: critical_path
observations: Sequence: schema.py → (diagnostics + firm_config + promote_seed in parallel) → parser migration → generator migration → (printable accessibility redesign + docxtpl+SDT Word + PDF completion + GUI tabs in parallel) → OCR integration.
~6-8 serialized session-equivalents with parallelism opportunities. Not the 11-15 arbitrary count initially proposed.

Tradeoff-analysis weighting: heaviest sessions are docxtpl+SDT (rank 1, burden 1.62), GUI transcription (rank 2), OCR integration (rank 3), schema.py (rank 4). Lightest: promote_seed refinement, firm config.
schema.py delivered: 10 integration tests passing. Consolidates 17 prefix-marked TGv3 decisions into Pydantic models.

Tier-based execution: Tier 1 (parallel post-schema: firm_config first, then diagnostics + promote_seed); Tier 2 (serial migration: parser then generator); Tier 3 (parallel production surfaces); Tier 4 (GUI and OCR heavy surfaces); Tier 5 (doculyze-core cross-repo extraction, deferred).

name: library_selections
observations: geopy wrapping Nominatim: selected for address geocoding over Google Maps. Licensing (OSM-compatible), free tier, adequate for firm scale. Adopt-as-dependency.
FDIC Institution Directory API: selected as sole data source for corporate trustee catalog. Authoritative, free, no authentication, stable schema with trust-powers filter. Adopt-direct.

Library recon outcomes use one of three resolutions: adopt-as-dependency (library is swappable, chosen for specific reasons), adopt-direct (no wrapping, used via its native API), or wrap (library is adopted behind a project interface for future substitutability).
SQLite as persistence backend: substitutable; any persistent store with geographic query support would serve. Not a coupled binding.

pydantic-settings v2.14.0 (released 2026-04-20, MIT, Python >=3.10): selected as the firm_config loader and validator. Provides native TomlConfigSettingsSource and YamlConfigSettingsSource, customizable source precedence via settings_customise_sources, env-var nested overlays via env_nested_delimiter, and nested Pydantic BaseModel support. Resolution: adopt-as-dependency. Rationale: unifies file load, env override, and field validation in one well-maintained package; source precedence hook is the right seam for injecting test fixtures.

stdlib tomllib (Python 3.11+, PSF license, read-only): selected as the TOML reader backing pydantic-settings' TomlConfigSettingsSource. Read-only limitation is non-binding because firm_config writes are a GUI-scope concern; hand-edits preserve their own comments by file semantics. Resolution: adopt-direct (via pydantic-settings). Rationale: zero dependency cost for read path; TOML 1.0.0 compliant. When a write path is needed (GUI config editor), tomlkit is the expected companion choice but that is a future decision.

ruamel.yaml (0.19.x, MIT, Python 3.9-3.14): NOT adopted for firm_config. Remains the selection for diagnostic rule files (out of current scope) where YAML round-trip comment preservation is justified by rule authoring ergonomics. Caveat recorded for future rule-file writers: ruamel.yaml preserves comments and key order but normalizes scalar representations (booleans, None, indentation detail) even in round-trip mode — it is not a byte-exact editor.

Format decision for firm_config: TOML over YAML. Rationale: (1) stdlib reader eliminates a dependency for the read path; (2) TOML's key=value + table syntax has less footgun surface than YAML's indentation-significant grammar for attorney hand-editing; (3) firm_config content is predominantly scalar values under shallow nested tables, a shape TOML handles without friction; (4) pydantic-settings integration is first-class. YAML remains the right choice for diagnostic rule files where inline expressions and comments interleave densely.

Pydantic v2 native model_json_schema() + GenerateJsonSchema subclass + per-field Field(json_schema_extra=...) selected as the JSON Schema generation mechanism for editor-side validation of TOML config files. Resolution: adopt-direct (no new dependency; pydantic is already in dep tree). Rationale: emits draft-2020-12 which tombi supports; subclass hook supports root-level vendor extensions (x-tombi-toml-version, x-tombi-table-keys-order, x-tombi-string-formats); per-field schema overrides via WithJsonSchema handle Decimal-to-number coercion needed for tombi format validation.

pydantic-to-schema (aorumbayev) and check-jsonschema evaluated and NOT adopted for editor-schema generation workflow. pydantic-to-schema last released 2020, no tombi-extension hook, wrapper thinner than our needs. check-jsonschema is for CI-side TOML-against-schema validation, redundant with tombi's edit-time validation and Pydantic's load-time validation. datamodel-code-generator and json-schema-to-pydantic both reverse the direction (schema->model); not applicable.

ollama (>=0.6.1, Apache-2.0, Python >=3.8): selected as the official Python client for Ollama in TGv3 OCR backend. Resolution: adopt-as-dependency. Rationale: official package tracking the Ollama core release cadence; thin surface (14.4 kB wheel; depends only on httpx and pydantic, both already first-class in v3); native Pydantic-schema delivery via format=Schema.model_json_schema(); sync and async clients available. Disambiguation hazard: the third-party PyPI package `ollama-python` (last release 2024-01, four total releases) is abandoned and must not be selected. Import name is `ollama`.

Ollama structured-output mechanism: GBNF grammar-constrained decoding inherited from llama.cpp; JSON schemas are auto-converted to grammars via the json-schema-to-grammar module and constraints apply at every token via logit masking, not post-hoc retry. Implication for any TGv3 component using Ollama with structured output: a string-typed reasoning channel declared first in the Pydantic schema is the current best-practice posture for materializing chain-of-thought benefit, since constrained decoding generates fields in schema declaration order. Pydantic v2 model_json_schema preserves declaration order, making this disciplined ordering achievable without additional tooling.

anthropic Python SDK (>= pin set at plan execution, MIT, Python >=3.8): selected as the production OCR backend client (4.3b AnthropicBackend). Resolution: adopt-as-dependency. Rationale: official SDK from Anthropic; supports PDF document content blocks (no rasterization step), extended thinking, prompt caching with cache_control breakpoints, and both tool_use and output_config structured-output mechanisms. The pin lands at plan execution; the plan-authoring step verifies the SDK version supports all four features plus the output_config + extended thinking combination (Anthropic docs are silent on this combination's compatibility rather than affirming it). GA structured outputs require Claude Opus 4.5+ / Sonnet 4.5+ / Haiku 4.5; older models constrain the backend to tool_use mode only.

name: rule_engine_binding
observations: rule-engine library (PyPI package, BSD-3 license). Safe expression evaluation via a custom Python-like grammar; no use of Python's eval or exec internally. Supports type-resolver context for structured inputs.

Coupling rationale: diagnostic rule syntax (YAML files authored by paralegals) is defined in terms of rule-engine's expression grammar. Swapping libraries would require redesigning the rule file format and retraining paralegals on new syntax.
Integration shape: DiagnosticRule wrapper class loads rule YAML, constructs a rule-engine Rule with TrustData+FirmConfig context, evaluates on demand, emits Diagnostic instance on match.
Debug REPL available via `python -m rule_engine.debug_repl` for paralegal rule testing.

Wrap resolution: TGv3 wraps rule-engine behind two constructs rather than adopting its API directly. build_eval_context(trust, config, ref_date) -> dict composes TrustData and FirmConfig into a unified {trust, firm, now} namespace via Pydantic's model_dump(mode='python'). DiagnosticRule is a Pydantic model carrying the compiled rule_engine.Rule as a PrivateAttr. Rule expressions evaluate against the derived dict via rule-engine's default resolve_item resolver; no custom Context resolver is required.

Rule construction is performed at loader time immediately after Pydantic validates the YAML entry, not deferred to first evaluation. Construction-time exceptions (RuleSyntaxError, RegexSyntaxError, AttributeResolutionError) are caught and wrapped as DiagnosticConfigError with file and rule-code attribution. Runtime-only exceptions (SymbolResolutionError, EvaluationError) are handled by the evaluator as meta-diagnostics with codes engine.symbol_unknown and engine.eval_error rather than propagated as exceptions.

Type-resolver posture for v1: top-level symbols (trust, firm, now) are declared DataType.UNDEFINED via rule_engine.type_resolver_from_dict. This catches unknown-symbol typos (rule-engine raises SymbolResolutionError) without forcing exhaustive leaf-type declarations. Per-leaf tightening (e.g., trust.elections.estate_value_approximate: FLOAT) is deferred until the rule corpus motivates the discipline.

Pydantic-to-rule-engine integration constraints that shape the wrap: (a) model_dump() strips plain @property values (only @computed_field-decorated properties serialize), so TGv3's collected_total_value, beneficiary_shares_total, etc. are injected into the eval context via explicit getattr in build_eval_context; (b) methods on Pydantic models are unreachable from rule expressions regardless of resolver choice, so TrustData.minor_beneficiaries(ref_date) is pre-computed and exposed as a dict key; (c) model_dump(mode='python') returns enum instances, not strings, but for str-mixin enums like TrustType(str, Enum) the instance is-a str via inheritance, so rule-engine's == against string literals (trust.trust_id.trust_type == 'individual') works correctly.

name: python_stack_commitments
observations: Python >=3.12 floor. Required for PEP 695 type alias syntax (type Foo = ...) used in relationship enum unions.

Pydantic v2.x as data-modeling library. Uses ConfigDict, field_validator (with mode='before' for coercion), model_validator (mode='after' for cross-field constraints), populate_by_name=True for alias handling.
stdlib datetime.date only; no third-party date library (pendulum, arrow, etc.). Integrates cleanly with Pydantic v2.

Pydantic idioms are cross-cutting conventions that apply across all design entities; they live in project instructions rather than as graph observations to avoid duplication or artificial traversal requirements.

name: library_reconnaissance_process
observations: Library reconnaissance precedes every design session for components with plausible existing library coverage. Outcome documented per component: adopt / wrap / build-custom with rationale.
Reconnaissance targets specific properties: feature match, maintenance status, license compatibility, ecosystem compatibility (Python >=3.12, Pydantic v2, pixi).
Principle: avoid reinventing poorly, under-budgeting capability, and over-budgeting effort. Reaching for mature libraries first prevents all three failure modes.

Reconnaissance is a distributed activity feeding each design session, not a separate session. Outcomes persist in library_selections (swappable choices) or as infrastructure entities (coupled bindings).

Three negative recon outcomes recorded by the firm-config loader: deepmerge/mergedeep rejected for deep-merge utility (custom 12-line implementation preferred over per-strategy library config); atomicwrites/portalocker rejected for atomic file writes (stdlib os.replace + tempfile sufficient); platformdirs/appdirs rejected for cache directory resolution (manual platform branching consistent with adjacent v3 code). All three subsystems use stdlib only.

name: audit_log_persistence
observations: Destination: shared SharePoint document library at https://crosbycrosbyllp.sharepoint.com/sites/internal-applications/Shared Documents/trust-generator/, a Teams-backed channel folder under the internal-applications Microsoft Team's SharePoint site. Maintainer-owned (site was provisioned by Team creation). Readers access via SharePoint web view; .jsonl files render as plain text with one JSON record per line. Reader access pattern is incident triage: an investigator navigates to users/<upn>/logs/ for the paralegal who prepared the trust under investigation and inspects the month-scoped file.

Mechanism: the OneDrive sync client mounts the trust-generator folder on each workstation at ~/Crosby and Crosby LLP/internal-applications - trust-generator/. The audit log writer uses stdlib open('a') against a Path; the sync client uploads asynchronously. Path A (sync client) was chosen over Path B (Microsoft Graph API) because sync-client adoption keeps the writer free of authentication, credential rotation, and retry logic. Path B's server-side atomicity would be the only reason to prefer it, and concurrency isolation is achieved structurally by the subfolder design, not by atomicity guarantees.

Concurrency isolation is structural. Audit records land at <sync_root>/users/<upn>/logs/audit-YYYY-MM.jsonl where <upn> is the paralegal's M365 account prefix. Per-user subfolders guarantee that no two workstations ever target the same file, eliminating both the Windows O_APPEND-over-SMB interleaving risk and the OneDrive sync client's conflict-copy behavior. The users/ subtree's organization also anticipates future per-user synchronized artifacts (drafts, custom rules) landing alongside logs without structural reshape.

firm.toml surface this layer requires: (a) new [user] section with a non-empty upn field; (b) tilde expansion added to load_firm_config()'s path-resolution pass (Path(value).expanduser() applied before the existing relative-to-absolute transformation); (c) loader-side ${user.upn} post-parse substitution in diagnostics.audit_log_dir (not a TOML language feature — a string replacement the loader performs after validating the UPN). These additions are prerequisites; the diagnostics engine cannot run without them.

Per-workstation deployment prerequisites (the workstation must satisfy these before the engine's audit log can function): paralegal clicks Sync on the SharePoint library in a browser; sets 'Always keep on this device' on the synced folder to prevent online-only placeholders from breaking open('a') append semantics; verifies .jsonl is not blocked by tenant-level extension policy (fallback: .log extension with unchanged JSONL content); maintainer sets [user] upn in firm.toml. The writer creates users/<upn>/logs/ on first override via Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); the directory itself does not require pre-provisioning.

Identity source rationale: firm.toml [user] upn is the explicit identity declaration. Rejected alternatives: (a) stdlib getpass.getuser() / whoami because local Windows usernames across the firm's workstations are inconsistent (generic hostnames like CROSBY-PC, mixed conventions including spaces) and not trustworthy as identity; (b) whoami /upn because machines are not Entra-joined (command returns 'not a domain user'); (c) Microsoft Graph /me endpoint because it imposes the Path B dependency tree the persistence mechanism was chosen to avoid. Population pre-onboarding: hand-set by the maintainer. Population post-onboarding: captured by the future paralegal-onboarding workflow.

The firm_config_loader introduced in 2026-04-28 mirrors this layer's users/<upn>/logs/ SharePoint subtree convention with a parallel firm/config/ subtree for the shared firm-wide TOML, both under the same library root. The two subtrees coexist without coupling: the loader does not consume audit-log content; the audit-log writer does not consume firm-config content beyond what load_firm_config() already exposes via FirmConfig.diagnostics.audit_log_dir.

Forward chore from firm_config_loader: the override-record audit log this layer writes (and which diagnostics_enforcement references in its observation #1) must be amended to capture full effective configuration per decision. Currently captures restriction_level only; required additions are effective threshold values (single_soft, joint_soft, single_hard, joint_hard, approaching_cliff_ratio) and the substituted audit_log_dir path. Until this lands, forensic reconstruction of threshold policy at decision time depends on cross-referencing SharePoint version history with audit-record timestamps.

name: ocr_extraction_design
observations: OCR extraction in TGv3 produces a TrustData paired with a sidecar ExtractionTrace; the trace carries per-field provenance, illegibility flags, and verification state, while TrustData remains validation-uniform. The architectural alternatives — strict α (OCR populates QuestionnaireSeed directly) and strict β (OCR uses a third bounded context) — were rejected: α reintroduces conditional-validation-within-a-single-model at the Seed layer, β invents a new bounded context the Seed-vs-TrustData split already addresses.

The OCR extraction surface is a parser variant. OCR populates TrustData like the (reference-only legacy v2) docx, json, and pdf parsers, with the trace as the only meaningful structural addition. There is no 'OCR-specific bounded context' in TGv3; the extraction discipline lives in the parser's return shape, not in the data model.

The diagnostics engine has two emission sources after this design lands: rule-driven (declarative YAML, evaluated against eval_context by the rule-engine library) and trace-driven (procedural, synthesized from ExtractionTrace state). The split is a deliberate architectural seam, not a workaround. Per-field fan-out cannot be expressed in the rule-engine library's expression model (one expression evaluates against one context dict). Future Diagnostic-emitting features choose which side they live on; the seam is permanent vocabulary.

The model output strategy is structurally constrained free generation. The vision-language model's output schema reserves a string-typed reasoning channel and per-field illegible/note structure alongside data fields; output is constrained at the token level via grammar-constrained decoding. Plain constrained generation without a reasoning channel was rejected because it forces hallucination on illegible inputs (the model has nowhere structured to put 'no'). Plain free generation without schema constraint was rejected because malformed-JSON repair loops add tail-latency without recovering reasoning quality.

Verify and override are distinct paralegal actions with distinct semantics. Verify is per-field, low-friction, mutates the trace, requires no audit record at v3.0. Override is per-generation-event, high-friction (≥10-character reason), writes a force_generation audit record, allows generation to proceed despite remaining diagnostics. A field can be both verified (transcription confirmed) and reside on a trust that is overridden (generation forced past unrelated business-rule diagnostics); the actions do not interact.

Confidence quantification is deferred. The trace's per-field confidence slot is reserved as a typed marker (Annotated[float, RawSelfReport] | None) but not populated by any v3.0 backend. A future ConfidenceProtocol implementation populates the slot. The deferral is a v3.0 commitment to scalar raw self-report semantics; alternative encodings (probability distribution, enum tier, calibrated logit) are explicitly outside scope for the slot's definition.

Re-extraction (running OCR multiple times on the same source) and trace merging are out of scope for v3.0. Each extract call produces a fresh ExtractionResult; reconciling traces from multiple runs (with potentially different field indexing) is its own design problem and earns its own session if it lands.

OCR extraction has two concrete backends: OllamaBackend (dev-only, local inference, GBNF grammar-constrained decoding) and AnthropicBackend (production-facing, hosted Claude API, native structured-output mechanism). The two produce identical ExtractionTrace shapes — the trace contract is the cross-backend invariant — but their envelope schemas and mapper functions are intentionally forked. The 'structurally constrained free generation' observation describing a string-typed reasoning channel applies to OllamaBackend only; AnthropicBackend uses extended thinking as an out-of-band channel and omits the reasoning field from its envelope entirely.

AnthropicBackend (4.3b Plan A) defaults the structured-output mechanism to `output_config` rather than tool_use. Rationale: Anthropic's API forbids combining forced `tool_choice={"type": "tool", ...}` with extended thinking. Plan A's posture is always-on extended thinking + `output_config` (the combination's API-level compatibility is plan-authoring-verified, not docs-affirmed); tool_use is preserved as a fallback under `tool_choice="auto"` with refusal mapped to ExtractionError. Plan B (deferred session) layers adaptive thinking-on-retry on this baseline.

name: firm_config_loader
observations: Single public entry point load_firm_config(local_path, shared_path) returning FirmConfig. Two-arg signature replaces predecessor single-path form with no compatibility shim.

Resolves two TOML files (shared firm-wide, hosted on SharePoint at ~/Crosby and Crosby LLP/internal-applications - trust-generator/firm/config/firm.toml; local per-workstation, repo-relative config/firm.toml). Each has a three-step discovery chain: explicit arg, env var (TGV3_FIRM_CONFIG / TGV3_FIRM_SHARED_CONFIG), convention.

Merge contract is recursive deep-merge: tables descend, lists EXTEND shared-first verbatim with no dedup, scalars overwrite verbatim, empty TOML literals treated as unset on the local side. Type mismatches surface at Pydantic validation.

Cache fallback layer at %LOCALAPPDATA%/trust-generator/firm.shared.cache.toml (Windows) or ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/trust-generator/firm.shared.cache.toml (POSIX). Verbatim-byte atomic writes after successful validation. Helper returns tuple[bytes, dict, bool] for TOCTOU-free cache-write gating.

Four-case fallback dispatch: case 1 happy-path, case 2 availability (missing/OSError), case 3 empty-bytes (OneDrive placeholder), case 4 integrity (TOML parse error). Cases 2 and 3 emit SharedConfigStalenessWarning; case 4 emits SharedConfigIntegrityWarning. Both warning classes are public.
Partial-sync completeness check via _SHARED_REQUIRED_SECTIONS = {firm, estate_thresholds, diagnostics} enforced after parse, before merge. Missing required sections route to integrity-fallback.

Shared-side relative paths rejected via introspective walk over Path-typed fields. Local-side relative paths resolve against the local file's parent directory. ${user.upn} substitution scoped to diagnostics.audit_log_dir only.

name: parser_post_promotion_protocol
observations: v3 parsers fill INTO a seed-initialized TrustData rather than constructing one from scratch. The seed-initialized TrustData arrives from promote_seed(seed); parsers must honor the one-shot-initializer invariant by never re-invoking promote_seed.

On parser-driven mutation of trust_id.trust_type (questionnaire reveals a different trust type than the seed): caller invokes _resolve_captions(new_trust_type) and updates both grantor_caption and co_grantor_caption. If transitioning into a state where co_grantor should exist (JT or MR) and co_grantor is None, materialize as GrantorInfo(). If co_grantor is already populated with fill data, preserve it.
On parser-driven mutation of trust_id.marital_status: adjust co_grantor per the same materialization rule. Captions remain unchanged because captions depend only on trust_type.

The JSON parser is exempt from the seed-initialized merge protocol because a JSON dump of TrustData is itself authoritative end-state; the JSON parser returns a fresh validated TrustData and the caller is responsible for reconciling against any in-progress seed if applicable.

name: parser_coercion_patterns
observations: v3 parsers absorb the v2-to-v3 type-shift surface. v2 schema fields are predominantly str defaults; v3 schema fields are typed (date | None, Decimal, Address, PersonReference, enums). Parser modules own the string-to-typed coercion before TrustData validation runs.

Date coercion: parsers accept the questionnaire's MM/DD/YYYY placeholder format and ISO YYYY-MM-DD for JSON; failed parses leave the field as None and emit a Python logging warning. Pydantic's field_validator(mode='before') is intentionally NOT relied on for date coercion because the parser's coercion failure path emits a warning rather than raising; Pydantic-level coercion would short-circuit this.

Decimal coercion: parsers strip currency symbols, percentage signs, and whitespace before constructing Decimal. A failed Decimal(...) constructor leaves asset-value fields at Decimal(0) (warning) and drops share-percent rows entirely (warning), preserving the meaningfulness of Decimal(0) in surviving share-percent rows.

Address coercion: parsers map v2's free-text address strings into the v3 Address model via best-effort splitting on commas. Each part populates the corresponding field. Geocoding (latitude/longitude) is NOT performed at parse time; the geocoder runs separately.

PersonReference coercion: parsers populate full_legal_name from the v2 string. The two-token name validator on full_legal_name raises ValidationError on one-token names; the parser traps and re-constructs as PersonReference(is_entity=True, entity_name=value, full_legal_name=''). CorporateTrustee discrimination uses a conservative case-insensitive regex (Bank|Trust Company|Trust Department|N.A.|LLC|LLP|Corporation|Corp.|Inc.|Insurance Co) on the name; matches yield CorporateTrustee instances with INFO logging per discriminated entry.

BeneficiaryShare/SpecificBequest reference coercion: parsers always emit recipient_external because v2 input has no id surface; later GUI work may refactor to recipient_ref when an id assignment workflow is built. Disinheritance resolution runs as a post-merge step that name-matches the v2 exclusions string against populated beneficiary lists in fixed iteration order (children, then descendants, then other_beneficiaries; Pydantic insertion order within each list); first match wins, multi-match logs WARNING.
